CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten warned President Donald Trump on Wednesday that his unprecedented Republican midterm convention won’t be as popular as he thinks, as the two-day event is scheduled for the same exact days as the first two NFL games of the season.

He continued Wednesday, “You can just see it by the fact that they’re doing it when the football season is starting. Who does that? My god. And when you look at the numbers, no, that is not the part of the party in which you actually need to motivate.”

The data guru went on to cite a recent CNN-SSRS poll showing 60% of Democrats are “extremely motivated” to cast their ballots in the upcoming midterms, while only 59% of MAGA Republicans — and a mere 41% of non-MAGA Republicans — expressed the desire.

“The ones who are not motivated to vote are the non-MAGA Republicans,” explained Enten. “The people who are far less likely to approve of Donald Trump, the people who think that Donald Trump’s Republican Party probably should be the end of it.”

He continued, “That’s where the problem is. So no, it is not, in fact, the hardcore Republican base that needs that motivation. It is other folks that this convention, simply put, won’t be reaching — because they’ll probably be watching football, like most Americans.”

The first-ever GOP midterm convention is taking place in Dallas, Texas, on Wednesday and Thursday. With Trump facing disastrous approval ratings amid a nationwide affordability crisis and his unpopular Iran war, many Republican midterm candidates have decided not to attend.

Enten certainly has a point regarding scheduling, as the defending Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks, are taking on the New England Patriots in a rematch Wednesday evening — and the Los Angeles Rams are playing the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday.

Enten went even further in arguing why Trump’s prior appeal isn’t helping: He cited a CNBC poll showing 52% are less likely to vote for a candidate endorsed by Trump, with only 29% more likely to — but only 50% less likely to vote for a democratic socialist.

The poll also showed 32% are more inclined to support a democratic socialist.

“So no, it’s not a good argument. This whole idea is ill-conceived,” said Enten, adding: “If you’re coming at it from, ‘Oh, you know, Trump is so good and those dem socialists are so bad,’ the American people are just like, ‘Actually, not quite right.’”
